_comment: THE CEILING IS THE BOARD'S OWN NUMBER -- a board that needs SIX HUNDRED AND EIGHTY-FIVE.
Session 22 raised the COMBO OFF iteration ceiling from the search's shared 60 to a constant 400
and recorded, as its open item 3: 'The ceiling is a constant (400), not the computed dig+kill
need. FlickerGoOffCount has the exact number at the clamp site; making the ceiling BE it is two
lines and removes a magic number.' This fixture is the board that makes the difference real.
It is built at the DECK'S OWN LIMIT, not beyond it:
* the loop is Emiel the Blessed ({3}, pip-free) blinking Cloud of Faeries (untaps TWO);
* the two best yields are Conservatory+Overgrowth (3) and Brushland (1, and it is the board's
only {C}, so the {C}-starved promotion takes that slot) -- refund 4 against a cost of 3, i.e.
net +1 a pass and net_c +1. One mana an iteration is this deck's thinnest live loop;
* the ONLY repeatable draw is an Investigate, which costs its {4} activation PLUS the Clue's
own {2} crack: SIX mana a card, the dearest draw in the decklist;
* the Living Wish is at library index 51 of 53, so the dig is 52 cards = 312 mana;
* the kill is Dimensional Infiltrator ({1}{U} -- Kitchen is the blue) exiling a 53-card
opponent library at {1}{C} = 106 mana and 53 colourless PIPS.
Total real work: 312 + 4 (wish + finisher) + 106 = 422 mana at ONE a pass. Four hundred
iterations cannot buy it, and no constant chosen against a different board ever could.
MEASURED, one binary:
default              -> 'blink Cloud of Faeries x685 -- COMBO OFF: wins this turn', VERIFIED,
and the harness's independent re-apply through the public
TurnSolver::ApplyPlan kills the opponent.
MTG_COMBO_OFF_EXACT_ITER=0 (Session 22's flat 400) -> x400, 'COMBO OFF (NOT PROVEN -- may not
finish)', and the re-apply leaves the opponent on 20 with 53 cards.
MTG_COMBO_OFF_MAX_ITER=60 -> ABSENT (the pre-Session-22 shared cap).
685 is larger than the 422 the board really needs, and that is the sizing being honest rather
than lucky: FlickerGoOffCount treats the dig and the kill as SEQUENTIAL PHASES and adds their
counts (MTG_EDF_GOFF_PHASES), so it asks for dig_iters + pip_iters. Over-sizing is safe by
ApplyBlinkLoop's standing contract -- it re-prices every activation and stops at the first it
cannot pay -- and a failed trial is rolled back whole. Under-sizing costs the whole kill, which
is what the 400 arm above demonstrates.
